subject: Post-call: Clearcrest budget alignment & pilot next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap — token economics, batching levers, and pilot next steps

Hi Avery —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and have clear next steps. I tried to capture the pain, the success criteria, and the cost levers we discussed.

Summary of pain & goals
- Real-time customer support triage is costing ~ $0.06 per inference today; you want to get that under $0.02 while keeping >95% intent accuracy.
- Peak latency SLO is 150ms for simple classification routes and ~350ms for multi-turn assistant flows.
- Budget constraint: pilot budget is $60k over 90 days; review committee prefers clear TCO with three scenarios (baseline / optimized / committed).

Cost/TCO levers we discussed (high level)
- Model selection: small distill models for classification (2–4x cheaper per token) vs mid-sized for assistant flows.
- Batching: synchronous micro-batching for classification endpoints (2–5x throughput improvement depending on QPS), see notes below.
- KV prefix caching: saving ~30–60% of decoder tokens for canned responses and common prefixes.
- Quantization: int4 path for non-sensitive embeddings/assistant flows (quality tests required).
- Routing: cost-aware routing to cheaper model variant for low-confidence fallbacks.

Assumptions used for rough ROI math (we’ll refine in the deck)
- Average 1.2k requests/day in pilot, average token output per request 45 tokens.
- Baseline cost estimate (your current infra) used as anchor: $0.06 per inference.
- Expected optimized stack (batching + cache + model swap) reduces per-inference cost by ~55% in our simulation.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) You to share the 90-day pilot budget doc and any procurement constraints (payment terms, PO requirements).
2) Redwood to deliver a 1-page TCO snapshot and a 6-slide pilot plan by Wed 12/23. We’ll include conservative and aggressive savings scenarios and the minimal guardrails for latency SLAs.
3) Technical deep-dive: schedule a 45m session with your infra/MLOps team the week of 12/27 (Ben to lead).
4) If budget fits, we’ll produce an SOW + pilot SLI targets and aim for an in-flight start by mid-Jan.

Attachments included: Redwood_TCO_Slides_v2.pptx (preview deck) — draft; will tune after we get your budget doc.

If any of the bullets above miss something important, flag and I’ll update.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
